# bitwrench

> Build web UIs from plain JavaScript objects. 165 KB on disk
> (45 KB gzipped), zero dependencies, no build step.

## What bitwrench is

bitwrench is a UI library where every element -- a button, a card, a full
page layout -- is a plain JS object called a TACO: {t, a, c, o} (Tag,
Attributes, Content, Options). You describe UI as data, and bitwrench
renders it to live DOM or HTML strings. It ships 47 ready-made components
(tables, cards, modals, tabs, forms, charts), a palette-based theming
system, client-side routing, and server-driven UI via SSE (bwserve).

## How it came to exist

bitwrench started in 2011 -- by an author who'd previously co-founded the
Lampdesk webVM that became Palm/HP webOS -- with a simple premise:
JavaScript objects should be the UI primitive, not markup strings. Where
Bootstrap required writing HTML and bolting on behavior separately, TACO
keeps tag, attributes, content, and behavior in one object. JSX went the
other direction (markup-first, toolchain required); bitwrench bets that the
object-first approach is more composable and needs zero tooling. That same
design choice happens to work everywhere from cloud dashboards to ESP32
microcontrollers.

## Lifecycle

1. **Define** -- write a TACO object: `{t, a, c, o}`
2. **Create** -- `bw.create(taco)` builds a real DOM element
3. **Hydrate** -- handles attach to `el.bw`, slots wire getters/setters, UUID assigned, state initialized
4. **Mount** -- element inserted into document; `o.mounted(el)` fires
5. **Interact** -- external code calls `el.bw.method()` -- the component updates its own DOM
6. **Unmount** -- `bw.unmount(el)` fires `o.unmount(el)`, tears down subscriptions, removes element

This is NOT a thin wrapper around the DOM. bitwrench replaces the entire
workflow: rendering, components, styling, state, theming, routing, and
server-driven UI. If you find yourself reaching for document.querySelector,
innerHTML, or hand-written CSS classes, you are fighting the library
instead of using it. Read the mental model below before writing code.

## The Mental Model (read this first)

bitwrench is closer to Qt/MFC than to React or jQuery. The key differences:

1. **UI is data, not strings.** You never write HTML strings or template
   literals. Every element is a JS object: `{t: 'div', a: {class: 'card'},
   c: 'Hello'}`. Nest them, loop them with .map(), branch with ternaries.

2. **Components are functions that return objects.** A "component" is just
   a function that returns a TACO. bitwrench ships 47 ready-made ones
   (bw.makeCard, bw.makeTable, bw.makeModal, etc.). Check BCCL first --
   if there is a built-in component for what you need, use it.

3. **Styling is generated, not hand-written.** Call `bw.loadStyles({
   primary: '#336699', secondary: '#cc6633' })` and bitwrench generates a
   full palette with hover/active/focus states for every color, plus
   structural CSS for all built-in components. For custom CSS, use
   `bw.css({'.myclass': {color: palette.primary.base}})` -- never raw
   CSS string literals.

4. **State is explicit, not reactive.** There is no virtual DOM and no
   automatic re-rendering. You change state, then call `bw.refresh(el)`.
   Or use handle methods: `el.bw.setTitle('new')`. Components own their
   DOM and update it directly.

5. **Events go in attributes.** `{t: 'button', a: {onclick: fn}, c: 'Go'}`
   -- never addEventListener in lifecycle hooks. Handlers in attributes
   survive re-renders; addEventListener in o.mounted does not.

For a complete progressive walkthrough, read `docs/thinking-in-bitwrench.md`.
For a compact code-first tutorial, read `docs/llm-bitwrench-guide.md`.

## Common Mistakes (and what to do instead)

### Mistake 1: Raw DOM manipulation

```javascript
// WRONG -- bypasses bitwrench entirely
document.getElementById('app').innerHTML = '<div class="card"><h2>Title</h2></div>';
var el = document.querySelector('.card');
el.style.background = '#f5f5f5';

// RIGHT -- bitwrench owns the DOM
bw.DOM('#app', bw.makeCard({ title: 'Title' }));
```

### Mistake 2: Hand-writing CSS

```javascript
// WRONG -- hard-coded colors, no theme integration
bw.injectCSS('.sidebar { background: #f5f5f5; border-right: 1px solid #ddd; color: #333; }');

// RIGHT -- CSS derived from palette, theme-switches automatically
var p = styles.palette;
bw.injectCSS(bw.css({
  '.sidebar': { background: p.surfaceAlt, border: '1px solid ' + p.light.border, color: p.dark.base }
}));
```

### Mistake 3: Hand-coding reactivity

```javascript
// WRONG -- manually tracking state and updating DOM nodes
var count = 0;
document.getElementById('counter').textContent = count;
document.getElementById('btn').addEventListener('click', function() {
  count++;
  document.getElementById('counter').textContent = count;
});

// RIGHT -- stateful TACO with explicit refresh
bw.DOM('#app', {
  t: 'div',
  o: {
    state: { count: 0 },
    render: function(el, state) {
      bw.DOM(el, { t: 'div', c: [
        { t: 'span', c: 'Count: ' + state.count },
        bw.makeButton({ text: '+1', onclick: function() {
          state.count++;
          bw.refresh(el);
        }})
      ]});
    }
  }
});
```

### Mistake 4: Building components that already exist

```javascript
// WRONG -- hand-building a table
{ t: 'table', c: [
  { t: 'thead', c: { t: 'tr', c: columns.map(function(c) { return { t: 'th', c: c }; }) } },
  { t: 'tbody', c: rows.map(function(r) { return { t: 'tr', c: ... }; }) }
]}

// RIGHT -- bitwrench has a sortable, paginated table component
bw.makeTable({ data: rows, columns: columns, sortable: true, pageSize: 20 })
```

bitwrench ships 47 components: cards, tables, modals, toasts, tabs,
accordions, carousels, forms, navigation, charts, and more. Check
`docs/component-cheatsheet.md` or `docs/component-library.md` before
building from scratch.

### Mistake 5: addEventListener in lifecycle hooks

```javascript
// WRONG -- lost on re-render
{ t: 'button', c: 'Save',
  o: { mounted: function(el) { el.addEventListener('click', save); } } }

// RIGHT -- survives re-render
{ t: 'button', a: { onclick: save }, c: 'Save' }
// or using BCCL:
bw.makeButton({ text: 'Save', onclick: save })
```

### Mistake 6: `data-*` attributes for binding

<!-- drift-lint:ignore-start: migration note must name the retired attribute -->
bitwrench uses no `data-*` attributes. `data-bw-action` existed in bwserve by
mistake and was removed in v2.1.0. Server-driven click handling uses
`bw_act_*` class tokens: `{ t: 'button', a: { class: 'bw_act_save' } }`.
<!-- drift-lint:ignore-end -->

## Quick Start

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bitwrench@2/dist/bitwrench.umd.min.js"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <div id="app"></div>
  <script>
    bw.loadStyles({ primary: '#336699', secondary: '#cc6633' });

    bw.DOM('#app', {
      t: 'div', a: { class: 'bw_container' },
      c: [
        bw.makeNavbar({ brand: 'My App', items: [{ text: 'Home', href: '#' }] }),
        bw.makeCard({ title: 'Hello', content: 'Built with bitwrench.' }),
        bw.makeTable({ data: [
          { name: 'Alice', role: 'Admin' },
          { name: 'Bob', role: 'User' }
        ], sortable: true })
      ]
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

No build step. No npm. Open the file in a browser.

## TACO Format

```javascript
{
  t: 'div',                         // tag (defaults to 'div' if omitted)
  a: { class: 'card', id: 'x' },   // attributes (including event handlers)
  c: [                              // content: string, TACO, or array
    { t: 'h2', c: 'Title' },
    { t: 'p', c: 'Body' }
  ],
  o: {                              // options (lifecycle, state -- never in HTML output)
    state: { count: 0 },
    render: function(el, state) { /* re-render on bw.refresh(el) */ },
    handle: { reset: function(el) { /* el.bw.reset() */ } },
    slots: { title: '.title' },     // => el.bw.setTitle() / el.bw.getTitle()
    mounted: function(el) { },      // after DOM insertion (NOT for event handlers)
    unmount: function(el) { }       // before DOM removal
  }
}
```

Content is HTML-escaped by default. Use `bw.raw(str)` for trusted HTML.

## Rendering Functions

| Function | Returns | Use When |
|----------|---------|----------|
| bw.DOM(sel, taco) | void | Mount into existing container |
| bw.mount(sel, taco) | root element | Need el.bw handle/slot access |
| bw.create(taco) | detached element | Building elements before inserting |
| bw.html(taco) | HTML string | SSR, emails, Node.js, CLI |

## Styling

```javascript
// 1. Load structural CSS (component styles, layout classes)
bw.loadStyles();

// 2. Load themed CSS from seed colors (generates full palette)
var styles = bw.loadStyles({ primary: '#336699', secondary: '#cc6633' });
var p = styles.palette;

// 3. Write custom CSS using palette values
bw.injectCSS(bw.css({
  '.my-sidebar': { background: p.surfaceAlt, color: p.dark.base },
  '@media (max-width: 768px)': { '.my-sidebar': { display: 'none' } }
}));

// 4. Dark mode
bw.toggleThemeMode();   // switch between primary and alternate palettes
```

Palette keys: primary, secondary, tertiary, success, danger, warning, info,
light, dark (all objects with .base, .hover, .active, .light, .darkText,
.border, .focus, .textOn). Also: surface, surfaceAlt, background (plain
strings, not objects).

## State and Updates

Three levels of interactivity -- use the simplest that fits:

1. **Static TACO**: plain objects, no state. Most UI is this.
2. **Re-render on demand**: call bw.DOM() again when data changes.
3. **Stateful TACO**: o.state + o.render + bw.refresh().

For targeted updates without full re-render, use handles and slots:

```javascript
var el = bw.mount('#app', bw.makeCard({ title: 'Stats', content: '0' }));
el.bw.setTitle('Revenue');      // slot setter -- updates just the title
el.bw.setContent({ t: 'b', c: '$42k' });  // content can be a TACO too
```
